name: bounded canonical-base64 text envelope for small binary-semantic payloads
goal: Preserve and replay exact finite octet semantics using ordinary low-volume repository text transport, without LFS, artifact/package storage, hosted compute, external object storage, paid/trial credits or manual-user execution.

public_basis.rfc4648: RFC 4648 sections 3.2-3.5 and 4: base64 represents arbitrary octet sequences; padding is required unless a referring specification says otherwise; non-alphabet characters are rejected by default; conforming encoders set pad bits to zero so a canonical encoding exists.
public_basis.github_repository_limits: GitHub repository limits documentation recommends single objects <=1 MB and directory width <=3000, with a 100 MB enforced single-object limit. This protocol chooses bounds far below the recommendation and uses only ordinary repository text objects.

closed_format.encoding: RFC4648 base64, standard alphabet, padding required when applicable, no whitespace or line wrapping, canonical zero pad bits
closed_format.manifest: small JSON naming contiguous chunk indices, repository paths, observed Git blob SHAs, encoded-character counts and decoded-octet counts
closed_format.chunking: split only on octet boundaries; each chunk independently canonical; chunks are immutable after publication

publication_and_replay: Create each canonical base64 chunk as UTF-8 text and read it back; record its observed repository blob SHA.
Create manifest only after every chunk readback succeeds.
CAS/readback the small publication pointer or role-local checkpoint that names the manifest.
Replay by fetching the named manifest and exact chunk paths/blobs in index order. Missing, changed, duplicate or out-of-order chunk is FAIL, never guessed/repaired.

For semantic preservation, canonical base64 text plus immutable repository identity uniquely denotes the octet sequence. If an outcome requires an actual byte file, executable loader, binary attachment API or platform-specific consumer, this protocol alone is UNSUPPORTED rather than a handoff.
strict_checks: manifest and chunk size bounds hold
fetched blob SHA exactly equals manifest claim
base64 contains only the RFC4648 alphabet plus legal terminal '=' padding; no whitespace or ignored characters
encoded length is a multiple of 4
padding count/decoded length agree and unused pad bits are zero
canonical re-encoding of decoded octets equals stored chunk text exactly
concatenated decoded length equals manifest total

acceptance_boundary.PASS: The material outcome is durable preservation/replay/comparison of a small exact octet sequence and canonical textual representation is an acceptable carrier.
acceptance_boundary.UNSUPPORTED: The material outcome specifically requires a binary file/attachment/object to be emitted or consumed by an unavailable environment/API, requires arbitrary code/dependency execution, exceeds the conservative low-volume bounds, or depends on protected authority.
acceptance_boundary.REJECT: Any route whose steady state requires LFS, artifact/package storage, hosted runners, cloud/object storage, paid/trial/monthly credits, or manual user conversion.

quota_and_cost.repository_transport: ordinary low-volume text API only; tolerate rate limits via checkpoint/backoff; API volume is not used as compute

scope_note: This is a bounded semantic-preservation mechanism, not a general binary artifact service. Git history may retain prior text versions; the protocol concerns exact current-tree content and replay semantics.
